newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific Railroad CEO resigns.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific Railroad CEO resigns.

text.p: Union Pacific Corp said Wednesday Ronald J. Burns has resigned as chief executive officer and president of Union Pacific Railroad Co.
Union Pacific spokesman Gary F. Schuster declined to comment on the company's statement, which noted Burns joined the Omaha, Neb.-based railroad in August of 1995 from Enron Corp.
The company said Jerry Davis, president of Southern Pacific Rail Lines, was named president and chief operating officer of the railroad, replacing Burns.
It said Dick Davidson, president and chief operating officer of Union Pacific Corp and chairman of the railroad, was named chief executive of the railroad.
Davidson is scheduled to become chairman and chief executive of Union Pacific Corp January 1, succeeding Drew Lewis, the company pointed out.
It also noted Davis was executive vice president- operations at Union Pacific Railroad when it merged with the Missouri Pacific in 1983.
Davis and Davidson, his counterpart at the former Missouri Pacific, worked together on the merger, the company said.
"We are very fortunate to have someone with Jerry's working knowledge of the Union Pacific and Southern Pacific rail systems to step in as we merge the two lines," Lewis said.

"Jerry Davis is basically a lifelong employee of the Union Pacific," Davidson said. "When you add up his experience with us and at Southern Pacific and his operational knowledge of the railroad industry, Jerry is prepared to lead us through the merger."

Davis left Union Pacific in 1989 to become president of CSX Corp's CSX Rail Transport. In 1995, Davis joined Southern Pacific as its president and chief executive, where he remained until the Union Pacific/Southern Pacific merger was completed on September 11.
